title: Microfluidic Flow Chambers Using Reconstituted Blood to Model Hemostasis and Platelet Transfusion In Vitro
protocol: Vortex the collagen suspension vigorously and dilute it in isotonic glucose solution to a final concentration of 50 µg/ml.
Take a new disposable biochip from the provider's container.
Pipette 0.8 μl into the lane(s) of the microfluidic biochip on one end of the chip and mark as outlet.
Ensure that the lane is filled 5/6th with the collagen containing coating solution.
Make sure there are no air bubbles in the lane.
Incubate channels at 4 °C for 4 hr or overnight in a humidified and closed container.
Pipette blocking buffer into coated channels and mark as inlet.
Ensure the lane is completely filled with blocking buffer, avoiding air bubbles.
Cut tubing to equal lengths (12 cm).
Connect each tubing stretch with a pin.
Rinse tubing with distilled water using a syringe and 26 G needle.
Saturate the tubing with blocking buffer.
Store in a closed and humidified container for at least 1 hr.
Rinse the pump and manifold with distilled water, removing air bubbles.
Aspirate blocking buffer out of biochip lanes using a fixed 10 μl tip at the outlet.
Clean the surface of the biochip with a precision dust-free wipe and denatured alcohol to remove prints and dust.
Fix the biochip on an automated microscope stage.
Connect the eight-lane manifold splitter to the biochip outlet if multiple lanes are used simultaneously.
Collect fresh whole blood from a healthy volunteer in an evacuated tube containing heparin as an anticoagulant.
Place the tubes on a rotator pending blood reconstitution.
Complete the assay within 3 hours of phlebotomy.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 250 g to prepare platelet rich plasma (PRP).
Do not use the centrifuge brake to prevent disturbance of the loosely packed pellet.
Pool blood in a single conical centrifugation tube if more than one tube was collected.
Remove and discard the PRP and buffy coat.
Yield packed red blood cells with few platelets.
Thaw blood group AB (Rhesus D negative) plasma at 37 °C for 5 min and 20 sec per 4 ml.
Determine the hematocrit of the packed red blood cells using an automated hematology analyzer.
Determine the platelet concentration in the blood bank prepared platelet concentrate.
Calculate the volume of packed red blood cells and platelet concentrate to yield 40% hematocrit and 250 x 10³ platelets/µl in a 1 ml sample.
Transfer packed red blood cells and plasma into a fresh tube using a clipped pipet tip.
Add platelet concentrate until the sample volume reaches 1 ml.
Gently mix the reconstituted blood by inverting.
Perform a complete blood count (CBC).
Replace the volume of platelet fraction with an equal volume of 0.9% sodium chloride in water to create a "blank" control sample.
Label and pipette 1 ml of reconstituted blood into a test tube containing 1 µl of 5 mM Calcein AM for a final concentration of 5 μM.
Mix gently by inverting the test tube.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at 37°C prior to use.
Mix the samples gently by inverting.
Position the samples next to the biochip on the automated stage.
Place tubing connected with the inlet of the biochip into the test tubes containing reconstituted blood samples.
Launch the pump at 50 dyne/cm² for channels linked to test tubes with reconstituted blood samples using the software of the pump.
Record images every 15 seconds for 5 minutes in real-time using the acquisition and experiment software of the microscope.
Wash out all tubing attached to the outlet with distilled water.
Follow the distilled water wash by washing with sodium hypochlorite (bleach) 0.5% (v/v).
Finally, wash with 0.1 M NaOH in water.
Discard the tubing pinned to the biochip inlet as hazardous waste.
Determine thrombus growth kinetics using image analysis software.
Open the plugin Image Analysis to determine surface coverage of platelets.
Set the fluorescence threshold in the Analyze Interactive tab to define pixel intensity correlating with a positive signal, i.e., adhered platelet or adhering platelets.
Use Create Tables to automatically generate a spreadsheet containing separate surface areas (in µm²) of "objects" containing pixels with signal between selected thresholds for each time point.
